issues.description: The differential validation run shows the golden (expert-correct) submission is REJECTED by evaluate.py: FR1, FR3, FR4 fail with 'missing PROBE for cycle 0' / 'missing PROBE for collision cycle 0', despite the README claiming the race condition between stimulus loading and DUT driving was fixed via a single initial block. The tb_regfile.v file shown still appears to exhibit the missing cycle-0 probe bug (or evaluate.py's stimulus/reference indexing is misaligned with the TB's actual probe timing), causing the documented fix to not actually resolve the issue in practice.
issues.evidence:
golden_run.stdout: '[TEST] FAIL: FR1: missing PROBE for cycle 0
[TEST] PASS: FR2
[TEST] FAIL: FR3: missing PROBE for collision cycle 0
[TEST] FAIL: FR4: missing PROBE for cycle 0' with golden_run.ok=false, expected=pass

issues.description: Since the golden submission fails, the benchmark case is not usable as-is: a correct participant answer would be marked incorrect, making the task unfair and the mutation/discrimination testing meaningless (requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0 and mutation_status is blocked_by_differential).
issues.evidence: validation report: 'mutation_status': 'blocked_by_differential', 'requirement_discrimination_coverage_score': 0.0, issue 'golden_rejected': 'evaluate.py rejects the expert golden solution (PASS expected)'

issues.description: Repeated retry of the tester produced the identical failure signature, indicating the bug is deterministic and not a flaky race — the claimed fix (merging load and drive into one initial block) is not actually effective or not correctly reflected in the artifact bundle used for grading.
issues.evidence: preflight.attempt_history shows two attempts with identical failure_signature '119799e3be217408ae53c846cc8b0ffbb65be8c1bad2127b73089ce8e54e9cef'

recommendations: Fix evaluation/tb_regfile.v (or evaluate.py's stimulus/probe indexing) so that the golden reference submission passes all requirements — the cycle-0 and collision-cycle-0 probe loss must be root-caused and eliminated, not just documented as fixed.

Re-run the differential validation (golden vs. naive-stub vs. at least one intentionally-flawed submission for each SR) after the fix to confirm golden passes with exit 0 and all baselines fail as expected.
Add a regression test to the harness itself (or a CI gate) that runs the golden submission through evaluate.py and asserts exit code 0 before shipping the benchmark case.

Verify that PROBE_MID-based SR1 check and SR3 reset check are not incidentally passing only because upstream probes are missing (i.e., re-validate all metrics once cycle-0 probes are restored, since functional_equivalence and cycle_accurate_match_rate were computed against an incomplete probe set).
